title: Navigation API: What happens when returning to entries captured by the navigation API

labels.name: topic: navigation API
labels.description: Topics directly related to the navigation API

body:
> [!NOTE]
> 🤖 **This issue was filed by an AI agent** (Claude, running in the [Pi](https://github.com/badlogic/pi-mono) coding agent) on behalf of @yoavweiss, migrating still-live issues out of [WICG/navigation-api](https://github.com/WICG/navigation-api) before that repository is archived. The migration scope was agreed with @noamr.
>
> This is a **migration of an existing discussion, not a new proposal**. The original author is credited below and the original thread is linked. Filed for triage — cc @noamr.

**Migrated from:** WICG/navigation-api#99 — filed by @jakearchibald (2021-04). 19 comments. Originally came out of whatwg/html#6207.

---

### The scenario

1. Page is `/`.
2. User clicks a link to `/article-1`, handled in-document via the `navigate` event.
3. User presses reload, or navigates away and comes back (no bfcache).
4. User presses back.

Existing `pushState` behaviour at step 4 is: switch URL and state to `/` with **no fetch**.

### The problem

`/article-1` may be a minimal document (just HTML and CSS for the article), while `/` is the full app shell capable of doing those in-document transitions. After the reload at step 3, the document that's loaded is `/article-1` — which is **not prepared to handle an in-document change to `/`**. The back button then puts the app in a state its own code never anticipated.

The original issue questioned how obvious this is to developers, and floated the alternative:

> 3. `/article-1` fetched and displayed.
> 4. `/` fetched and displayed.

i.e. entries that were previously same-document become cross-document. That's inconsistent in its own way, but arguably matches what each document can actually handle.

This is a semantics question about same-document entries surviving a document swap, not a feature request, which is why it's worth carrying over.

Related: WICG/navigation-api#289 (migrated separately) is the same class of problem — a same-document entry being traversed to by a document with no handler registered.

cc @jakearchibald @domenic
